title: Production Guardrails at Scale
objective: After this lesson you will be able to layer input validation, scope rules, PII redaction, output filters, and rate limits for production traffic — with attack gold items proving each layer and denied-attempt intelligence feeding back.
why: Prompt 101 taught guardrails for single bots; production multiplies attackers, traffic, and blast radius. A returns bot serving thousands faces crafted exfiltration daily, PII in every other ticket, and cost attacks via context stuffing. Production guardrails are layered systems with metrics per layer — defense in depth, measured per layer, attacked in gold.

blocks.text: Five layers, each with a job

**Input validation** (shapes, sizes, patterns — reject absurdities free). **Scope rules** (named sources + abstention, Prompt 101 Ch.6). **PII redaction** (detect + mask before model/logs — emails, cards, IDs). **Output filters** (block disallowed content classes post-generation). **Rate limits** (per-user/tenant/API-key quotas against cost attacks and brute probes). Each layer independent (one failing doesn't collapse others), each logged (denied attempts are threat signal).

blocks.caption: Validate → scope-check → redact → throttle: independent layers, shared log

blocks.text: PII: detect, mask, never log raw

Tickets contain emails, card numbers, addresses, IDs — all flowing into prompts, logs, and eval datasets unless redacted. Redact **before** model calls *and* before logging (logs are the forgotten exfiltration vector: PII in plaintext logs violates retention policies silently). Patterns per class (email/card/phone/ID), quarantine on novel shapes, and eval datasets scrubbed identically — gold sets with live PII are liabilities.
Rate limits as security, not just cost

Quotas per user/tenant/key bound three threats: cost attacks (context stuffing at scale), brute probing (injection fuzzing needs volume), and noisy-neighbor starvation (one tenant eating shared capacity). Tier quotas by trust (new users strict, established looser), return honest 429s with retry guidance, and alert on quota-exhaustion patterns (campaigns look like spikes).

blocks.title: Run the layers
blocks.note: Run it: expect redacted-pass, injection-block, oversize-block, card-masked-pass — in order. Each layer independent: PII masking never blocks, injection never merely masks.

items: Five independent layers (validate/scope/redact/filter/throttle), each logged — failure isolated per layer
PII redacted pre-model AND pre-log; eval datasets scrubbed; novel shapes quarantined
Rate limits as security (cost/probe/starvation); quotas tiered by trust with honest 429s

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice pipeline on all four inputs and map layers. (b) Add an output-filter check (block 'guaranteed refund' phrasing) with a test. (c) Write the attack gold trio for this pipeline (injection, PII-laden, oversize) with expected layer verdicts.
hints: Mappings: redacted-pass (PII masked, flows) / injection-block / oversize-block / card-masked-pass.
Output filter: /guarantee(d)? refund/i on generated text → block + route to human edit (generation-side gate).
Attack gold: injection→input-block; PII ticket→redacted-pass (masking proven); 600-char→oversize-block. Layer verdicts asserted.
exercise.why: Layer mapping (which input trips which layer), output-side extension, and attack-gold pinning are the three guardrail judgments — each verified, with layers proven independently.
exercise.code: // Layer-probe pattern: one adversarial input per layer, verdicts asserted.

quiz.q: Logs contain full ticket text with emails and card numbers. Issue?
options: PII in plaintext logs: retention violation + breach surface — redact pre-logging, scrub eval sets identically
quiz.explain: Logs are the forgotten exfiltration vector: plaintext PII violates retention silently. Redact before model AND before logs.

quiz.q: Quota-exhaustion spike from one tenant at 3am. Reading + response?
options: Campaign signal: cost/probe/starvation attempt — hold quota, alert, review attempt logs before any change
quiz.explain: Spikes are threat intelligence until proven otherwise: quotas hold while logs get reviewed. Raising blindly funds attacks.

quiz.q: Single guardrail layer (long system prompt) for everything. Verdict?
options: Fragile monoculture: one bypass defeats all — independent layers (validate/scope/redact/filter/throttle) isolate failures
quiz.explain: Defense in depth exists because layers fail independently. Prompt-only protection collapses entirely on first bypass.

summary: Five independent logged layers, PII redacted pre-everything, quotas as security, attack gold per layer. Guardrails measured per layer, never assumed whole.
next: Walled and throttled — now visible: traces, dashboards, and alerts on behavior, not just errors. Next: observability.
